items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: George Shearing and I, and John Levy, Denzil Best; we had a quartet at a club called the Clique.

ctx.x: Well, maybe we could talk a little bit more about some of the people you were playing side-by-side with in the late ‘40’s. After you left Dorsey, I think for the last time, was your base New York for a little while, ‘cause you played with Bud Powell. Or they played with you, is really more appropriate.
Oh yeah. Yeah, George Shearing and I, and John Levy, Denzil Best; we had a quartet at a club called the Clique. This was the late ‘40’s, I guess.

items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: We recorded but the first thing we did we did some things on Discovery label and recorded some tunes and things on that, and then Buddy DeFranco had to leave

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, and that really ticked me off because everything was backwards, you know. We didn’t get paid on time, and when you had to travel no arrangements were being made for it, and nothing. Everybody was on their own, you know, and I didn’t like it. So

when they left to go to California, I decided I was going to quit. So I left that group and this was about the time that I was just sort of like floating around. I got a call to come down to Birdland to work, finish out a week with Buddy Rich. Buddy Rich had a big band. So I went down to Birdland and worked the week with Buddy Rich and George Shearing was playing opposite Buddy Rich. In other words, in those days, in Birdland, there might be three or four different acts. And in this case I think it was George…

I would think that, you know, for managing musicians, you had a really valuable experience doing everything that they do, you know, because now you know what kind of travel they need to have, what kind of arrangements need to be made.

items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Sarah Vaughan with her group, Shearing and Buddy DeFranco, all worked in the same place. We all were on that same bill.

ctx.x: Okay. And basically begin playing again at various clubs and spots?

Yeah. That’s all. Just whatever gigs came along. When I got the call which led to Shearing was from Jimmy Jones calling me to come and sit in with [the] Buddy Rich big band, which was working opposite Jimmy Jones and Sarah Vaughan’s group. George Shearing was in there also. This is the way it used to work. You had three or four different groups playing at a nightclub. At that time, this was Buddy Rich with a big band, Sarah Vaughan with her group, Shearing and Buddy DeFranco, all worked in the same place. We all…
